BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.
- General Warranty cap: starting position 25% / AUD 6,000,000. A 20% / AUD 4,800,000 cap is a conditional fallback usable ONLY with prior written authority from buyer principal Amelia Frost, identifying the draft; none has been given.

- General claims period: 24 months after Completion; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval (none given).

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel – Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Status:** Internal / privileged. Seller material treated as untrusted and reviewed against the Buyer Playbook.

## Headline

The Seller's package is not "fair and balanced" from our side. It departs from the playbook on nearly every protection point, and several departures compound: a reduced cap, inflated thresholds, a shortened claims period, and then a sweeping "all limitations apply to all Claims" clause that would pull title, fraud, tax, IP and the specific indemnities under the same ceiling. Several of the Seller's own disclosures (Bluefen, Riverlark, bonuses, Ironquay) also confirm that key conditions and deliverables are *not* in place, which strengthens our hand on the completion mechanics.

Two points first on authority: the Seller's 20% / AUD 4.8m cap and 18-month period happen to match our *fallback* positions. Those fallbacks may only be used with prior written authority from Amelia Frost identifying the draft. None has been given. We therefore respond at our starting positions (25% / AUD 6m; 24 months) and do not signal that the fallbacks exist.

---

## 1. Liability architecture

### 1.1 General cap – cl 12.1
- **Seller:** 20% / AUD 4,800,000.
- **Playbook:** 25% / AUD 6,000,000 opening; 20% only with written Frost authority (not given).
- **Position:** Reject; counter at 25% / AUD 6m. Do not describe 20% as acceptable in any form.

### 1.2 Thresholds – cl 12.2
- **Seller:** de minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; excess-only recovery.
- **Playbook:** de minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; first-dollar ("tipping") recovery.
- **Reasoning:** Each number is 5x our position, and "excess only" effectively gifts the Seller the first AUD 250,000 of every claim stack. On a AUD 24m deal with a 30%-revenue customer and a live data incident, a AUD 25,000 per-claim floor would screen out most realistic operational breaches entirely.
- **Position:** Reject on all three elements. Counter at 5,000 / 50,000 / first-dollar.

### 1.3 Time limits – cl 12.3 / 13
- **Seller:** 18 months for general warranty claims; plus a rule that any limitation "applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise".
- **Playbook:** 24 months (18 only with Frost approval – not given); fundamental/title at least six years; tax/IP open; fraud uncapped and untimed.
- **Reasoning:** The second sentence is the more dangerous one. It is a default-inward drafting device: anything we fail to expressly carve out is silently captured by the general regime. Combined with 1.4 and 1.5 below, it collapses the separate categories the playbook requires us to keep.
- **Position:** Counter at 24 months. Delete the "applies to all Claims" default and replace with the opposite default: limitations apply only to general Warranty Claims and only where expressly stated.

### 1.4 Fundamental / Title warranties
- **Seller:** Same caps and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity".
- **Playbook:** Separate regime – 100% of price, at least six years, outside basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
- **Reasoning:** "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason. Title to 100% of the shares is the entire consideration; a 20% cap on a title failure means we could pay AUD 24m and recover AUD 4.8m if the shares turn out not to be the Seller's to sell. This is a non-negotiable for the Buyer.
- **Position:** Reject. Insert a standalone Fundamental Warranty regime per playbook.

### 1.5 Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance – cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5
- **Seller:** Apply to "all Claims of any nature".
- **Playbook:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance; Title/Tax/IP/payment/covenant categories kept separate; no hidden general-regime override.
- **Reasoning:** As drafted, these clauses would (i) purport to limit fraud – which is contrary to policy and likely unenforceable in NSW in any event, but we do not want to litigate that; (ii) make the warranties the exclusive remedy, which would neuter the Ironquay indemnity, the bonus funding covenant, the Riverlark discharge obligation and the Bluefen condition; and (iii) through non-reliance, undercut any pre-contractual statements about the DD-006 incident or Bluefen's position.
- **Position:** Reject. Require an express, non-waivable fraud/wilful concealment/deliberate misconduct carve-out from every limitation; confirm the exclusive-remedy and non-reliance clauses do not touch specific indemnities, completion covenants, conditions or Fundamental Warranties.

---

## 2. Disclosure and knowledge

### 2.1 General disclosure – Sch 7 and Disclosure Letter paras 1.1–1.2
- **Seller:** Everything in the data room as at 22 September 2026 (DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records" are deemed disclosed.
- **Playbook:** Specific fair disclosure only; reject whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- **Reasoning:** Whole-data-room disclosure converts the warranties into a statement that "everything is as per the data room", shifting the burden of finding problems entirely to us. Public-register disclosure is open-ended – it includes documents we never saw. Note also para 1.4: the Seller "admits nothing" by disclosing, so it wants the protective effect of disclosure without any corresponding acknowledgement of the underlying issues.
- **Position:** Reject general disclosure. Accept only matters fairly disclosed in the Disclosure Letter with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter. Delete the public-register limb. Para 1.4 can stay only if disclosure is limited to specific matters.

### 2.2 Buyer knowledge – cl 8.3
- **Seller:** No claim for any matter the Buyer *or its advisers* knew about, including anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records.
- **Playbook:** Delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions. Any qualifier must reference named Seller knowledge persons plus reasonable enquiry, and never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- **Reasoning:** "Discoverable" is a constructive-knowledge test – it bars claims for things we *could* have found, which is the general disclosure problem in another form. Extending it to "advisers" imputes every adviser's file to us. Read together with cl 12.3's "all Claims" default, it would also bar title and fraud claims.
- **Position:** Delete cl 8.3 in full. If the Seller insists on any knowledge concept, it should be a Seller knowledge qualifier only (named individuals, after due enquiry), applied to specifically identified warranties, and expressly inapplicable to Fundamental Warranties, fraud and indemnities.

---

## 3. Completion-critical items – where the Seller's own disclosures help us

### 3.1 Bluefen consent – cl 3 / 6.3; Disclosure para 2
- **Seller:** Reasonable endeavours; condition satisfied on delivery of written consent.
- **Disclosure confirms:** No final written consent and no evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied as at the letter date. Bluefen is ~AUD 3.6m / ~30% of FY26 revenue.
- **Playbook:** Effective consent AND evidence that its conditions are met, before Completion. Delivery alone is not enough; reasonable endeavours is insufficient for a material customer.
- **Reasoning:** A consent "on delivery" that is subject to unsatisfied conditions is not a consent – it is a conditional letter. If the cl 11.3 conditions later fail, we have paid for a business with its largest customer able to walk. Reasonable endeavours lets the Seller fail the condition at modest cost; our risk is a third of revenue.
- **Position:** Condition precedent: unconditional Bluefen consent under cl 11.2 in agreed form, plus documentary evidence that each cl 11.3 condition has been satisfied or irrevocably waived by Bluefen, delivered before Completion. Seller obligation at all-reasonable-endeavours (or best-endeavours) with a long-stop date and Buyer termination right. The Seller's own para 2 disclosure supports our asking for this: they have conceded the gap.

### 3.2 Riverlark facility – cl 2 / 7; Disclosure para 3
- **Seller:** ~AUD 3.2m outstanding; release "following Completion".
- **Disclosure confirms:** Not repaid, no discharge of security in the data room; change-control at cl 8.1 and discharge at cl 9.2.
- **Playbook:** Current payout figure; direct repayment from Completion funds; effective security releases at Completion. A post-completion release requires an irrevocable bank undertaking and Frost approval.
- **Reasoning:** The deal is debt-free/cash-free. A post-completion release means we own a company carrying AUD 3.2m of secured debt, with a bank change-of-control trigger (cl 8.1) potentially crystallising on Completion, and no certainty the Seller will fund the discharge. That is a direct price leakage risk and a security-over-our-asset risk.
- **Position:** Require (i) a bank payout letter current to Completion; (ii) direction in the funds flow paying Riverlark directly from the purchase price; (iii) executed deed of release and PPSR/other security discharges delivered at Completion, or at minimum an irrevocable bank undertaking to release on receipt of the payout amount. Do not accept the post-completion structure without a Frost sign-off, which we should not seek unless the Seller moves on everything else.

### 3.3 Employee bonuses – funds flow; Disclosure para 5
- **Seller:** DD-005 AUD 420,000 closing bonuses "are a matter for the Seller" and not itemised.
- **Disclosure confirms:** Bonuses are triggered by Completion; they are not in the draft funds flow; the letter is silent on payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs.
- **Playbook:** AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs must be a specific line item or seller-funded; the funds flow must not silently exclude them.
- **Reasoning:** "A matter for the Seller" is not a contractual obligation. The bonuses are a liability of the Company (our target), triggered by *our* transaction. If they are not funded at Completion, the Company pays them after Completion out of our cash – a straightforward transfer of AUD 420,000-plus from Buyer to employees for the Seller's benefit. The on-costs (superannuation, payroll tax) are real and currently unquantified.
- **Position:** Insert as a specific line item in the funds flow, deducted from the price or paid by the Seller at Completion, including an on-cost gross-up (figure to be confirmed by our tax advisers – do not assume a number). Back with a Seller covenant and a specific indemnity for any shortfall.

### 3.4 Ironquay IP – cl 11.1; Disclosure para 4
- **Seller:** Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment and "adequate".
- **Disclosure confirms:** Under DD-004 cl 7.3, SOW3 Project Materials transfer only on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee; DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open; no receipt or confirmatory assignment on file; DD-010 is not independent bank verification.
- **Playbook:** Broaden the narrow indemnity while preserving the SOW3 cure; treat the AUD 180,000 as unverified either way.
- **Reasoning:** The exposure is not the AUD 180,000 – it is that the Company may not own the SOW3 Project Materials at all until payment clears. An indemnity for the payment amount does not cover loss of IP, inability to exploit it, or an Ironquay infringement claim. We also do not know whether the fee has in fact been paid; the Seller is right that DD-010 is not proof of non-payment, and we should not assert it either way.
- **Position:** (i) Seller to procure, before Completion, either cleared-funds evidence of SOW3 payment and a confirmatory assignment from Ironquay, or to pay the open amount and procure the assignment at Completion (the "cure"). (ii) Expand cl 11.1 to an indemnity for all loss arising from any failure of title to, or encumbrance on, the SOW3 Project Materials or any claim by Ironquay, not merely the SOW3 fee. (iii) Keep this indemnity outside the general cap, basket and knowledge bar.

---

## 4. Other disclosed matters

### 4.1 Export/privacy incident – cl 4.6 / Sch 6; Disclosure para 6
- **Seller:** "Preliminary operational matter", not expected to be material.
- **Disclosure confirms:** Download link sent to an unintended external address; ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, timestamps); unknown whether accessed; investigation preliminary; notification question unresolved; no loss amount.
- **Playbook:** Preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand either way.
- **Reasoning:** We should not accept the Seller's materiality characterisation, nor should we over-claim. The correct posture is process: the facts are unresolved and the Seller controls the investigation until Completion.
- **Position:** Pre-completion covenant requiring the Seller to (i) preserve all access logs and related records; (ii) complete and document the investigation (including whether the link was accessed and the final record scope); (iii) provide written updates and the investigation outcome before Completion; and (iv) make a reasoned, documented assessment on notification. Add a specific warranty on the accuracy and completeness of the DD-006 disclosure and a specific indemnity for loss from the incident, sized to actual loss, not a fixed sum. Keep it outside the general regime. We make no assertion of breach or quantum.

### 4.2 Sandbar supplier renewals – Disclosure para 8
- **Seller:** Ordinary-course operating costs.
- **Disclosure confirms:** Three renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000); letter does not say whether unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.
- **Playbook:** Assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- **Position:** Request DD-008 and DD-011 terms on timing, notice/termination rights and accrual status. Reserve the characterisation until reviewed. Do not concede "ordinary course" in the SPA definitions, and do not propose a deduction at this stage.

### 4.3 Office lease (para 7) and Mossvale (para 9)
Both disclosures are framed to say consent is not required on a *share* sale. That is plausible for a share sale, but we should confirm from the documents themselves (DD-007 lease notification clause; DD-009 assignment restriction and any change-of-control language) rather than rely on the Seller's reading. If notification is required under the lease, make it a Seller completion deliverable.

### 4.4 Title – Disclosure para 10
- **Seller:** Title evidenced by the DD-012 share register.
- **Disclosure concedes:** DD-012 is the Seller's source; it does not state the Buyer has verified it.
- **Playbook:** Independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence; DD-012 is an internal supplied source, not independent proof.
- **Position:** Require, as completion deliverables: current ASIC extracts for the Company and Seller; PPSR search confirming no security over the shares (and release of any Riverlark security that touches the shares); board minutes and any required Seller shareholder/board approvals; executed share transfer and updated register; certificate of title/share certificates or cancellation; and a Fundamental Warranty of unencumbered title and capacity on the separate regime in 1.4. We run these searches ourselves.

### 4.5 Tax / IP – "settled under the general regime"
- **Seller:** Tax and IP warranties fall under the general cap/basket/18-month regime.
- **Playbook:** OPEN. Assume no resolution and no unlimited liability.
- **Position:** Do not accept the characterisation as "settled". Respond that tax and IP remain open and are to be negotiated as separate categories with their own limits. We should not, at this stage, propose unlimited liability – but we should resist folding them into the 20%/18-month regime, which would be worse than any realistic outcome of a separate negotiation.

---

## 5. Pattern worth naming

The draft uses the same device repeatedly: a modest-looking headline term, followed by a default rule that expands its reach. Examples: 18 months → "applies to all Claims unless expressly stated"; data-room disclosure → "plus public records"; buyer knowledge → "or its advisers" and "discoverable". Our mark-up should reverse each default so that limitations apply only where expressly stated and only to general Warranty Claims. If we only negotiate the headline numbers and leave the default rules, we lose most of what the playbook protects.

---

## 6. Summary of recommendations

| # | Item | Seller position | Our response |
|---|------|-----------------|--------------|
| 1 | General cap (12.1) | 20% / AUD 4.8m | Reject; 25% / AUD 6m. No fallback authority exists. |
| 2 | Thresholds (12.2) | 25k / 250k / excess only | Reject; 5k / 50k / first dollar. |
| 3 | Claims period (12.3) | 18 months | Reject; 24 months. No fallback authority exists. |
| 4 | "All Claims" default (13) | Limits apply to everything unless carved out | Delete; reverse the default. |
| 5 | Fundamental/Title | Same as general | Separate regime: 100%, ≥6 years, outside basket/de minimis/knowledge. |
| 6 | Fraud / exclusive remedy / non-reliance (9.3, 12.8, 20.5) | Apply to all Claims | Non-waivable carve-out for fraud, wilful concealment, deliberate misconduct; exclude indemnities, covenants, conditions, Fundamental Warranties. |
| 7 | Disclosure (Sch 7, paras 1.1–1.2) | Whole data room + public registers | Specific fair disclosure only; delete general limbs. |
| 8 | Buyer knowledge (8.3) | Blanket, incl. advisers and "discoverable" | Delete. Seller-knowledge qualifier only, named persons, never for title/capacity/fraud/indemnities. |
| 9 | Bluefen (3 / 6.3) | Reasonable endeavours; satisfied on delivery | CP: unconditional consent + evidence cl 11.3 conditions met, before Completion; stronger endeavours; long-stop. |
| 10 | Riverlark (2 / 7) | Post-completion release | Payout letter; direct payment from Completion funds; releases at Completion. Post-completion only with irrevocable undertaking + Frost approval. |
| 11 | Bonuses (funds flow) | "Matter for the Seller"; not itemised | Specific line item for AUD 420k + on-costs, Seller-funded; covenant + indemnity. |
| 12 | Ironquay (11.1) | SOW3 payment only | Pre-completion cure (payment evidence + assignment); broaden indemnity to IP title/claims; outside general regime. |
| 13 | DD-006 incident (4.6 / Sch 6) | "Not material" | Log preservation, investigation, pre-completion updates, specific warranty and indemnity; no assertion of breach or quantum by us. |
| 14 | Sandbar renewals | Ordinary course | Assess DD-008/DD-011; reserve; no deduction yet. |
| 15 | Title (DD-012) | Share register sufficient | Independent ASIC/PPSR searches, approvals, executed transfer; Fundamental Warranty. |
| 16 | Tax / IP | "Settled" under general regime | Reject; remain open as separate categories; no unlimited liability proposed. |
| 17 | Lease / Mossvale | No consent needed | Verify from documents; lease notification as completion deliverable if required. |

**Immediate actions:** (a) issue a mark-up at the playbook starting positions on items 1–8; (b) convert items 9–12 into conditions precedent and completion deliverables, using the Seller's own paragraphs 2–5 of the Disclosure Letter as the basis; (c) order independent title and PPSR searches now; (d) request the DD-006 investigation status and the DD-008/DD-011 renewal terms; (e) confirm internally that no Frost authority has been sought for the fallback cap or period, so the team does not inadvertently signal flexibility.

- **Reasoning:** "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason. Title to 100% of the shares is the entire consideration; a 20% cap on a title failure means we could pay AUD 24m and recover AUD 4.8m if the shares turn out not to be the Seller's to sell. This is a non-negotiable for the Buyer.
- **Position:** Reject. Insert a standalone Fundamental Warranty regime per playbook.

### 1.5 Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance – cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5
- **Seller:** Apply to "all Claims of any nature".
- **Playbook:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance; Title/Tax/IP/payment/covenant categories kept separate; no hidden general-regime override.
- **Reasoning:** As drafted, these clauses would (i) purport to limit fraud – which is contrary to policy and likely unenforceable in NSW in any event, but we do not want to litigate that; (ii) make the warranties the exclusive remedy, which would neuter the Ironquay indemnity, the bonus funding covenant, the Riverlark discharge obligation and the Bluefen condition; and (iii) through non-reliance, undercut any pre-contractual statements about the DD-006 incident or Bluefen's position.
- **Position:** Reject. Require an express, non-waivable fraud/wilful concealment/deliberate misconduct carve-out from every limitation; confirm the exclusive-remedy and non-reliance clauses do not touch specific indemnities, completion covenants, conditions or Fundamental Warranties.

## 2. Disclosure and knowledge

### 2.1 General disclosure – Sch 7 and Disclosure Letter paras 1.1–1.2
- **Seller:** Everything in the data room as at 22 September 2026 (DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records" are deemed disclosed.
- **Playbook:** Specific fair disclosure only; reject whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- **Reasoning:** Whole-data-room disclosure converts the warranties into a statement that "everything is as per the data room", shifting the burden of finding problems entirely to us. Public-register disclosure is open-ended – it includes documents we never saw. Note also para 1.4: the Seller "admits nothing" by disclosing, so it wants the protective effect of disclosure without any corresponding acknowledgement of the underlying issues.
- **Position:** Reject general disclosure. Accept only matters fairly disclosed in the Disclosure Letter with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter. Delete the public-register limb. Para 1.4 can stay only if disclosure is limited to specific matters.

### 2.2 Buyer knowledge – cl 8.3
- **Seller:** No claim for any matter the Buyer *or its advisers* knew about, including anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records.
- **Playbook:** Delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions. Any qualifier must reference named Seller knowledge persons plus reasonable enquiry, and never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- **Reasoning:** "Discoverable" is a constructive-knowledge test – it bars claims for things we *could* have found, which is the general disclosure problem in another form. Extending it to "advisers" imputes every adviser's file to us. Read together with cl 12.3's "all Claims" default, it would also bar title and fraud claims.
- **Position:** Delete cl 8.3 in full. If the Seller insists on any knowledge concept, it should be a Seller knowledge qualifier only (named individuals, after due enquiry), applied to specifically identified warranties, and expressly inapplicable to Fundamental Warranties, fraud and indemnities.

## 3. Completion-critical items – where the Seller's own disclosures help us

### 3.1 Bluefen consent – cl 3 / 6.3; Disclosure para 2
- **Seller:** Reasonable endeavours; condition satisfied on delivery of written consent.
- **Disclosure confirms:** No final written consent and no evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied as at the letter date. Bluefen is ~AUD 3.6m / ~30% of FY26 revenue.
- **Playbook:** Effective consent AND evidence that its conditions are met, before Completion. Delivery alone is not enough; reasonable endeavours is insufficient for a material customer.
- **Reasoning:** A consent "on delivery" that is subject to unsatisfied conditions is not a consent – it is a conditional letter. If the cl 11.3 conditions later fail, we have paid for a business with its largest customer able to walk. Reasonable endeavours lets the Seller fail the condition at modest cost; our risk is a third of revenue.
- **Position:** Condition precedent: unconditional Bluefen consent under cl 11.2 in agreed form, plus documentary evidence that each cl 11.3 condition has been satisfied or irrevocably waived by Bluefen, delivered before Completion. Seller obligation at all-reasonable-endeavours (or best-endeavours) with a long-stop date and Buyer termination right. The Seller's own para 2 disclosure supports our asking for this: they have conceded the gap.

### 3.2 Riverlark facility – cl 2 / 7; Disclosure para 3
- **Seller:** ~AUD 3.2m outstanding; release "following Completion".
- **Disclosure confirms:** Not repaid, no discharge of security in the data room; change-control at cl 8.1 and discharge at cl 9.2.
- **Playbook:** Current payout figure; direct repayment from Completion funds; effective security releases at Completion. A post-completion release requires an irrevocable bank undertaking and Frost approval.
- **Reasoning:** The deal is debt-free/cash-free. A post-completion release means we own a company carrying AUD 3.2m of secured debt, with a bank change-of-control trigger (cl 8.1) potentially crystallising on Completion, and no certainty the Seller will fund the discharge. That is a direct price leakage risk and a security-over-our-asset risk.
- **Position:** Require (i) a bank payout letter current to Completion; (ii) direction in the funds flow paying Riverlark directly from the purchase price; (iii) executed deed of release and PPSR/other security discharges delivered at Completion, or at minimum an irrevocable bank undertaking to release on receipt of the payout amount. Do not accept the post-completion structure without a Frost sign-off, which we should not seek unless the Seller moves on everything else.

### 3.3 Employee bonuses – funds flow; Disclosure para 5
- **Seller:** DD-005 AUD 420,000 closing bonuses "are a matter for the Seller" and not itemised.
- **Disclosure confirms:** Bonuses are triggered by Completion; they are not in the draft funds flow; the letter is silent on payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs.
- **Playbook:** AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs must be a specific line item or seller-funded; the funds flow must not silently exclude them.
- **Reasoning:** "A matter for the Seller" is not a contractual obligation. The bonuses are a liability of the Company (our target), triggered by *our* transaction. If they are not funded at Completion, the Company pays them after Completion out of our cash – a straightforward transfer of AUD 420,000-plus from Buyer to employees for the Seller's benefit. The on-costs (superannuation, payroll tax) are real and currently unquantified.
- **Position:** Insert as a specific line item in the funds flow, deducted from the price or paid by the Seller at Completion, including an on-cost gross-up (figure to be confirmed by our tax advisers – do not assume a number). Back with a Seller covenant and a specific indemnity for any shortfall.

### 3.4 Ironquay IP – cl 11.1; Disclosure para 4
- **Seller:** Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment and "adequate".
- **Disclosure confirms:** Under DD-004 cl 7.3, SOW3 Project Materials transfer only on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee; DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open; no receipt or confirmatory assignment on file; DD-010 is not independent bank verification.
- **Playbook:** Broaden the narrow indemnity while preserving the SOW3 cure; treat the AUD 180,000 as unverified either way.
- **Reasoning:** The exposure is not the AUD 180,000 – it is that the Company may not own the SOW3 Project Materials at all until payment clears. An indemnity for the payment amount does not cover loss of IP, inability to exploit it, or an Ironquay infringement claim. We also do not know whether the fee has in fact been paid; the Seller is right that DD-010 is not proof of non-payment, and we should not assert it either way.
- **Position:** (i) Seller to procure, before Completion, either cleared-funds evidence of SOW3 payment and a confirmatory assignment from Ironquay, or to pay the open amount and procure the assignment at Completion (the "cure"). (ii) Expand cl 11.1 to an indemnity for all loss arising from any failure of title to, or encumbrance on, the SOW3 Project Materials or any claim by Ironquay, not merely the SOW3 fee. (iii) Keep this indemnity outside the general cap, basket and knowledge bar.

## 4. Other disclosed matters

### 4.1 Export/privacy incident – cl 4.6 / Sch 6; Disclosure para 6
- **Seller:** "Preliminary operational matter", not expected to be material.
- **Disclosure confirms:** Download link sent to an unintended external address; ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, timestamps); unknown whether accessed; investigation preliminary; notification question unresolved; no loss amount.
- **Playbook:** Preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand either way.
- **Reasoning:** We should not accept the Seller's materiality characterisation, nor should we over-claim. The correct posture is process: the facts are unresolved and the Seller controls the investigation until Completion.
- **Position:** Pre-completion covenant requiring the Seller to (i) preserve all access logs and related records; (ii) complete and document the investigation (including whether the link was accessed and the final record scope); (iii) provide written updates and the investigation outcome before Completion; and (iv) make a reasoned, documented assessment on notification. Add a specific warranty on the accuracy and completeness of the DD-006 disclosure and a specific indemnity for loss from the incident, sized to actual loss, not a fixed sum. Keep it outside the general regime. We make no assertion of breach or quantum.

### 4.2 Sandbar supplier renewals – Disclosure para 8
- **Seller:** Ordinary-course operating costs.
- **Disclosure confirms:** Three renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000); letter does not say whether unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.
- **Playbook:** Assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- **Position:** Request DD-008 and DD-011 terms on timing, notice/termination rights and accrual status. Reserve the characterisation until reviewed. Do not concede "ordinary course" in the SPA definitions, and do not propose a deduction at this stage.

### 4.3 Office lease (para 7) and Mossvale (para 9)
Both disclosures are framed to say consent is not required on a *share* sale. That is plausible for a share sale, but we should confirm from the documents themselves (DD-007 lease notification clause; DD-009 assignment restriction and any change-of-control language) rather than rely on the Seller's reading. If notification is required under the lease, make it a Seller completion deliverable.

### 4.4 Title – Disclosure para 10
- **Seller:** Title evidenced by the DD-012 share register.
- **Disclosure concedes:** DD-012 is the Seller's source; it does not state the Buyer has verified it.
- **Playbook:** Independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence; DD-012 is an internal supplied source, not independent proof.
- **Position:** Require, as completion deliverables: current ASIC extracts for the Company and Seller; PPSR search confirming no security over the shares (and release of any Riverlark security that touches the shares); board minutes and any required Seller shareholder/board approvals; executed share transfer and updated register; certificate of title/share certificates or cancellation; and a Fundamental Warranty of unencumbered title and capacity on the separate regime in 1.4. We run these searches ourselves.

### 4.5 Tax / IP – "settled under the general regime"
- **Seller:** Tax and IP warranties fall under the general cap/basket/18-month regime.
- **Playbook:** OPEN. Assume no resolution and no unlimited liability.
- **Position:** Do not accept the characterisation as "settled". Respond that tax and IP remain open and are to be negotiated as separate categories with their own limits. We should not, at this stage, propose unlimited liability – but we should resist folding them into the 20%/18-month regime, which would be worse than any realistic outcome of a separate negotiation.

## 5. Pattern worth naming

The draft uses the same device repeatedly: a modest-looking headline term, followed by a default rule that expands its reach. Examples: 18 months → "applies to all Claims unless expressly stated"; data-room disclosure → "plus public records"; buyer knowledge → "or its advisers" and "discoverable". Our mark-up should reverse each default so that limitations apply only where expressly stated and only to general Warranty Claims. If we only negotiate the headline numbers and leave the default rules, we lose most of what the playbook protects.
